interest: Cool 1934 and warm 1937 Italian receptions for Japanese cruisers.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.3365, covering May 1934 to August 1937) documents goodwill and training visits of Imperial Japanese Navy vessels to Italian ports. It consists of three primary records: a detailed consular report from Naples and a diplomatic despatch from Rome concerning the April 1934 visit of the training cruisers Asama and Iwate under Vice Admiral Hajime Matsushita, and an August 1937 despatch from Rome reporting on the visit of the cruisers Iwate and Yakumo under Admiral Mineichi Koga to Palermo, Naples, and Rome. Together, these reports track the operational and social itineraries of Japanese officers and midshipmen, assess the discipline and public impact of Japanese naval personnel in Italy, and chart the diplomatic evolution of Italo-Japanese relations from formal, reserved protocol in 1934 to privileged, high-profile royal and Fascist receptions in 1937 on the eve of Italy's accession to the Anti-Comintern Pact.
